steps.what: Enter the sale amount and tender type at the terminal.
Accept physical tender and assist customers with payment difficulties.
Check terminal status and record settlement at the till.

tasks.design: Test native terminal integration in the {OTHER} point-of-sale system first. Synchronize amounts and settlement references while retaining cashier checks and physical tender handling.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing terminal connectors may carry both amount and settlement status.
tasks.still_hard: Cash, vouchers and declined tenders still require human handling.
tasks.human_edge: Assist customers and recognize unusual tender situations.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate entry; payment authority stays unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: terminal integration can remove duplicate entry without replacing physical tender handling.

assumptions: Boundary is cashier work from agreed total to settlement; customer tender time and existing authorization runtime are excluded, unchanged and earn no saving. Receipt issuance is separate.
Till produces sale_id, amount, currency and tender_type; terminal produces transaction_id, amount and status. Missing connectors retain manual entry and status checks; no card credential extraction.
Native configuration is tested first. Shares and savings are provisional model knowledge, not measured.
unknowns: Tender mix and existing connector configuration.
research_questions: Does synchronization preserve clear failed and offline statuses?

incremental.description: Report connector mismatches and test tender defaults.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=82.5 gross=17.5 net=16.5 after 1 upkeep. Low: cash-heavy till; high: supported electronic tenders. Physical handling unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Issue receipts, refunds, credits and change.

steps.what: Retrieve the original sale and prepare the issuance amount and destination.
Inspect any returned item and authorize the exact proposed issuance.
Issue authorized receipts, refunds, credits or change to customers.

tasks.design: Configure original-sale lookup in the {OTHER} point-of-sale system before custom code. The cashier confirms the proposed amount and destination, then executes and hands over the authorized issuance; any edit voids confirmation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Original tender and sale details require separate lookup.
tasks.enabler_now: Native linked-sale records can prefill the issuance proposal.
tasks.still_hard: Return condition, policy exceptions and cash handover remain human.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve disputed returns and count physical change carefully.
tasks.altitude: Shorter retrieval; refund decision rights stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: original-sale lookup can prefill refund details; physical handover remains.

assumptions: Boundary covers issuance after payment or return request. Shares represent aggregate cashier effort across receipt, change and refund cases; return inspection is conditional.
Till supplies sale_id, lines, original_tender, refundable_balance, currency and destination; policy owner supplies dated return rules. Missing records use manual receipt lookup.
Native configuration first. Proposal v1 binds sale, items, amount, currency and destination. Editing requires new authorization. Only cases inside cashier delegation are modeled.
unknowns: Case mix, existing lookup and delegated limits.
research_questions: Can the till reject stale confirmations and duplicate refunds?

approvals.approved_version: issuance proposal v1: sale, items, amount, currency and destination; any edit voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=87.5 gross=12.5 net=11.5 after 1 upkeep. Low: mostly receipt-only transactions; high: frequent original-sale lookups. Inspection and issuance effort unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Answer customer questions and resolve complaints.

steps.what: Listen to the customer and clarify the issue.
Find applicable product information and current service policy.
Explain the answer and agree a remedy or referral.

tasks.design: Test indexed policy cards in {DOCS} and link current catalogue facts from the {OTHER} point-of-sale system. Fixed issue categories shorten lookup; the cashier still chooses applicable information and handles the conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policies and product details sit in different screens.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document search and category shortcuts can expose current sources.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous complaints and distress require listening and judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize frustration and negotiate an appropriate response.

ambition.what: Give unresolved complaints a clear referral explanation at checkout.

tasks.altitude: Less searching; complaint discretion stays unchanged.

reach.learn: Service limits and specialist referral routes.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: indexed policy cards can shorten factual lookup without automating complaints.

assumptions: Boundary ends at explanation or referral; refund execution is separate. Listening and remedy discussion remain unchanged.
Service owner supplies policy_id, category, effective_date, remedy_limit and source_link; merchandising supplies item_id and product facts. Missing fields retain manual source lookup.
Test native document search first. No recording or generated customer answer is proposed.
unknowns: Lookup time and completeness of current policy cards.
research_questions: Do category shortcuts improve correct-policy retrieval?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=90 gross=10 net=9 after 1 upkeep. Low: lookup already quick; high: fragmented policies. Customer conversation stays fully human.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Check expected cash balances at the checkout registers.
Observe queues and confirm available checkout colleagues.
Request cover or cash replenishment based on the observed situation.

tasks.design: Test native consolidated cash views in the {OTHER} point-of-sale system and configure low-float thresholds. Cashiers still observe queues and request assistance; expected cash is clearly distinguished from physical counts.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing tender ledgers can support consolidated expected-cash views.
tasks.still_hard: Physical shortages and colleague availability are not established by a ledger.
tasks.human_edge: Balance queues, colleagues needing breaks and cash security.

ambition.what: Review low-float warnings before each busy checkout period.

tasks.altitude: Less register checking; staffing and cash movement authority stays unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: ledger views consolidate expected register cash but cannot replace physical counts.

assumptions: Boundary ends at requests, excluding staff reassignment and cash transport. Those colleagues retain their work and receive no saving in this denominator.
Till supplies register_id, opening_float, cash_tenders, refunds, movements and timestamp; staff report availability verbally. Missing or stale feeds retain manual checks.
Native configuration first. Access and employee consultation under applicable national rules are included. No employee performance ranking is introduced.
unknowns: Movement record completeness and current consolidated views.
research_questions: Do expected-cash warnings identify actual low floats reliably?

incremental.description: Report stale feeds or misleading thresholds.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=87.5 gross=12.5 net=11.5 after 1 upkeep. Low: incomplete movement records; high: reliable feeds. Queue observation and requests retain all time.

role.altitude: Less screen switching while customers and physical cash remain central.
role.ambitious_version: A cashier who explains exceptions clearly and spots cash shortages early.
